chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from more than one narrator: they asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about menstruation and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding its time.

He said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله set forth regarding menstruation three sunnahs, in which he clarified every difficulty for whoever heard and understood them, such that he left no room for anyone to speak about it by personal opinion.

As for one of the sunnahs: it concerns the menstruating woman who has known days which she has counted without confusion, then she experiences istiḥāḍah and the blood continues with her while in that state she still knows her days and the extent of their number. A woman called Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubaysh had istiḥāḍah, so she came to Umm Salamah, and she asked the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله about that. He said: “She leaves the salat (prayer) for the measure of her periods, or the measure of her menstruation,” and he said: “It is only a gushing,” then he ordered her to perform ghusl, bind herself with a cloth, and pray.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “This is the sunnah of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله concerning the woman who knows the days of her periods and they have not become confused for her. Do you not see that he did not ask her how many days they were, nor did he say: if it exceeds such-and-such a number of days then you are in istiḥāḍah. Rather, he established for her known days, whether few or many, once she knows them. Likewise my father عليه السلام gave this ruling, and he was asked about the mustaḥāḍah, so he said: ‘That is only a gushing or a stroke from Shayṭān; so let her leave the salat (prayer) on the days of her periods, then perform ghusl and perform wudu (ablution) for every salat (prayer).’ It was said: even if it flows? He said: ‘Even if it flows like a waterspout.’”

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “This is the explanation of the hadith of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and it accords with it. This is the sunnah for the woman who knows the days of her periods, and she has no fixed time except her own days, whether they are few or many.

As for the sunnah of the woman who previously had established days, then they became confused for her due to prolonged bleeding, increasing and decreasing until she lost track of their number and their place in the month, then her sunnah is different from that. That is because Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubaysh came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said: ‘I have istiḥāḍah and do not become pure.’ The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘That is not menstruation; it is only a gushing. So when the menstruation approaches, leave the salat (prayer), and when it departs, wash the blood from yourself and pray.’ So she would perform ghusl at every salat (prayer), and she would sit in a basin belonging to her sister, and the yellowness of the blood would rise above the water.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Do you not hear that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded this one differently from how he commanded that one? Do you not see that he did not say to her: leave the salat (prayer) on the days of your periods; rather he said to her: ‘When the menstruation approaches, leave the salat (prayer), and when it departs, perform ghusl and pray.’ This shows that this was a woman whose days had become confused for her; she did not know their number or their time. Do you not hear her saying: ‘I have istiḥāḍah and do not become pure’? My father used to say: ‘She remained in istiḥāḍah for seven years.’ In less than that, doubt and confusion arise. For that reason she needed to recognize the onset of the blood from its departure, and the change of its color from black to something else, because menstrual blood is black and recognizable. Had she known her days, she would not have needed to know the color of the blood, because the sunnah regarding menstruation is that yellowness, murkiness, and what is above that during the days of menstruation, when she knows it to be menstruation, is all menstruation, whether the blood is black or otherwise. This clarifies to you that little blood and much blood during the days of menstruation is all menstruation when the days are known. But when she does not know the days and their number, she needs to observe the onset and cessation of the blood and the change in its color, then leave the salat (prayer) accordingly. And I do not see that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: sit out such-and-such number of days, and whatever exceeds that you are in istiḥāḍah, just as he did not command the first one in that way. Likewise my father عليه السلام gave a ruling in a similar case, for a woman from our family had istiḥāḍah and asked my father about that, and he said: ‘When you see the dark copious blood, leave the salat (prayer), and when you see purity, even for an hour in the daytime, perform ghusl and pray.’”

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “So I see my father’s answer here to be different from his answer regarding the first mustaḥāḍah. Do you not see that he said: ‘She leaves the salat (prayer) on the days of her periods,’ because he looked to the number of the days, whereas here he said: ‘When you see the dark copious blood, leave the salat (prayer),’ and here he commanded her to look at the blood when it comes, departs, and changes. His saying ‘al-baḥrānī’ is close in meaning to the saying of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘The blood of menstruation is recognizable.’ My father عليه السلام only called it baḥrānī because of its abundance and color. This is the sunnah of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله regarding the one whose days have become confused so that she does not know them, and she only knows them by the blood, whether the days are few or many.”

He said: “As for the third sunnah, it concerns the woman who has no previous established days and had never seen blood before, and she saw it at the first onset of maturity and it continued with her. The sunnah of this one is different from that of the first and second. That is because a woman called Ḥamnah bint Jaḥsh came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: ‘I have been afflicted with a severe menstruation-like bleeding.’ He said: ‘Use cotton padding.’ She said: ‘It is more severe than that; it pours forth profusely.’ So he said to her: ‘Bind yourself firmly and count yourself menstruating every month, in the knowledge of Allah, for six days or seven days. Then perform ghusl once, and fast twenty-three or twenty-four days, and perform ghusl for Fajr once, delay Ẓuhr and hasten ʿAṣr and perform ghusl once, and delay Maghrib and hasten ʿIshāʾ and perform ghusl once.’”

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “I see that he explained in this case something different from what he explained in the first and second, because her case differs from the case of those two. Do you not see that if her days had been fewer than seven, and were five or fewer than that, he would not have said to her: ‘Count yourself menstruating for seven,’ for then he would have ordered her to leave the salat (prayer) on days when she was in istiḥāḍah and not menstruating. Likewise, if her menstruation had been more than seven and her days were ten or more, he would not have ordered her to pray while she was menstruating. Among what further clarifies this is his saying to her: ‘Count yourself menstruating,’ for taḥayyuḍ only applies to a woman who is to be charged with what a menstruating woman does. Do you not see that he did not say to her in terms of known days: count yourself menstruating on the days of your menstruation? Also clarifying this is his saying to her: ‘in the knowledge of Allah,’ because she did have a reality known to Allah, even though all things are in the knowledge of Allah. This is clear and evident that this woman had never had established days before that at all. This is the sunnah for the woman with whom the blood continues at the very first time she sees it: the utmost of her period is seven, and the utmost of her purity is twenty-three, until she comes to have known days and then she moves to them.

Thus all the states of the mustaḥāḍah revolve around these three sunnahs; she is hardly ever outside one of them. If she has known days, whether few or many, then she follows her own days and the pattern established for her; there is no separately fixed number for her other than her own days. If the days become confused for her, advancing and delaying, and the blood changes colors for her, then her sunnah is to follow the onset and cessation of the blood and the change in its states. If she had no days before that and experienced istiḥāḍah the first time she saw blood, then her period is seven and her purity is twenty-three. If the blood continues with her for months, she acts in every month as he said to her. If the blood stops in fewer than seven or more than seven, then she performs ghusl the moment she sees purity and prays, and she remains like that until she sees what occurs in the second month. If the blood stops at its time from the first month in the same way until two or three menstruations occur consecutively for her, then it is now known that this has become for her a known time and pattern, so she acts upon it and leaves what is besides it, and that becomes her sunnah going forward if she experiences istiḥāḍah, until she comes to sit out her periods. The time was only established as two menstruations or three menstrual cycles consecutively because of the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to the woman who knows her days: ‘Leave the salat (prayer) on the days of your periods.’ We thereby knew that he did not make a single menstrual cycle a sunnah for her such that he would say: ‘Leave the salat (prayer) on the days of your one cycle,’ but rather he clarified periods in the plural, the least of which is two menstruations and upward. If her days become confused for her, increasing and decreasing until she cannot determine a limit from them, nor a color from the blood, then she acts according to the onset and cessation of the blood, and she has no sunnah other than this, due to the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘When the menstruation approaches, leave the salat (prayer), and when it departs, perform ghusl,’ and due to his saying صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘The blood of menstruation is black and recognizable,’ just as my father said: ‘When you see the dark copious blood.’ But if the matter is not like that, rather the blood overwhelms her and the istiḥāḍah continues incessantly while the blood remains upon one color and one state, then her sunnah is seven and twenty-three, because her case is the case of Ḥamnah when she said: ‘It pours forth profusely.’

key_terms.أَقْرَائِهَا: her menstrual periods or cycles by which her habitual days are known
key_terms.السُّنَنِ: the prophetic normative rulings or established patterns set forth in this matter
key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: ritual purity or cessation of bleeding at which worship resumes
key_terms.الِاسْتِحَاضَةُ: non-menstrual irregular bleeding that has distinct legal rulings
key_terms.الْبَحْرَانِيَّ: dark, abundant blood; a descriptive marker used to identify menstrual blood in context
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation; the legally recognized menstrual bleeding discussed in the ruling
key_terms.تَحَيَّضِي: count yourself as menstruating; a legal directive for one without an established prior cycle
key_terms.عَزْفٌ: a gushing flow; here used to describe istiḥāḍah rather than menstruation

ai.seo_question: What are the three prophetic rulings for menstruation and istiḥāḍah in Shiʿi hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out three prophetic sunnahs for distinguishing menstruation from istiḥāḍah: the ruling for a woman with known menstrual days, the ruling for one whose days have become confused and who must identify menstruation by the characteristics of the blood, and the ruling for one with no prior pattern whose bleeding began from the outset. It presents these as a complete legal framework in ritual purity and salat (prayer), grounded in the teachings of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and explained by Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.
